target: stipule (PO_0020041) part_of seedling (PO_0008037), pattern 12 (part of a qualified whole)
reason: This is the stipule of a seedling's leaves, a narrower use of stipule. It follows the earlier decisions on 'seedling leaf' and 'seedling leaflet', which used part_of seedling. Subulate, length and hairy all describe the stipule itself.

'Standard' is the Fabaceae banner petal (PO_0025324), but it is also the inner tepal of Iridaceae. The appendages being described (slender, 0.5 mm long, adnate, counted) are separate outgrowths, not a region of the banner. Mapping them to the banner or to its base would give the banner a length of 0.5 mm. No appendage class fits, and 'corolla appendage' was also rejected earlier.

target: the organ described (fruit, nutlet or seed, from context) with a count of furrows, handled like 'longitudinal ridge' and the rib counts in config/flora_counted_parts.tsv
reason: A furrow is a surface feature of the organ that has it, not a part with its own qualities. The only quality stated is a count ('each side with 5 transverse furrows'). This is the same case as 'longitudinal ridge', which was decided on 2026-11-14.

target: portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656)
reason: Exact: this is French for gland, and PO_0005656 has the synonym 'gland'. 'glands' was mapped to the same class on 2026-11-14. Glands placed on a lamina or petiole could later be refined to extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057) from context.

target: inflorescence (PO_0009049)
reason: Narrower: a group of spikelets is a partial inflorescence. This follows the 2026-11-14 decision mapping 'spikelet cluster' to inflorescence. The count, 'scattered' and 'patent' all describe the groups as wholes.

target: stipule lobe (FLOPO_0986076) at the basal position of the stipule (part of stipule PO_0020041)
reason: An auricle is an ear-shaped basal lobe. Orbicular, flared, persistent and 2.5-4 mm long all describe that lobe, so the existing stipule lobe class fits better than a new 'auricle' class. Leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) belongs to grass leaf sheaths and is not this structure.

target: bract apex (PO_0025154) part_of flower bract (PO_0009034), pattern 12
reason: This is the apex region of a flower bract, handled like 'phyllary apex' (bract apex part of involucral bract) on 2026-11-14. 'Acute' is an apex shape.

'Retinacle' is a variant of 'retinaculum', which was rejected on 2026-11-14 for the same reason. In Acanthaceae it is the hooked funicle (jaculator). In Apocynaceae and orchids it is part of the pollinarium. 'Straight, 5 mm long' suggests Acanthaceae, which would be funicle (PO_0020006), but only the family settles it.

target: sepal abaxial epidermis (PO_0006054)
reason: Exact under the surface rule. The outer surface of a sepal is its abaxial side, handled like 'leaf lower surface' (leaf lamina abaxial epidermis). Tomentose and pubescent are surface qualities.

target: phyllome lamina tooth (PO_0025515) part_of stipule (PO_0020041), pattern 12
reason: This is a tooth on a stipule. It follows the 'bract lobe' and 'lemma lobe' decisions, which used the generic phyllome lamina part with part_of the named phyllome. The length (0.1-0.2 mm) is the tooth's own length.

This is a position phrase cut off from its noun ('2 bracteoles at the base', '3 or 4 at the base'). The counted part is the bracteole or flower named before it, and the whole is the organ whose base is meant.

target: perianth (PO_0009058) part_of staminate flower (PO_0025600), pattern 12
reason: This is the perianth of a male flower. PO_0025600 has 'male flower' as a synonym. Hypocrateriform, campanulate, glabrate and length all describe the perianth.

This is a depression ('apical hollow 0.2 mm', '40-50 µm in diam.'), not a part, and the examples do not name the organ it is in. Seed, fruit apex and pollen are all possible. 'depression' was rejected for the same reason on 2026-11-14.

The examples describe nipple-like projections of two very different sizes, 1-1.5 mm and 190-250 µm. These are probably a fruit or capsule apex in one flora and a cell or seed-surface papilla in the other. The organ is not named, so no single target fits.

target: cotyledon (PO_0020030)
reason: Exact: plural of cotyledon. Collateral, plano-convex and free are qualities of the cotyledons.

Narrower, or a close relative. A short, swollen, lobed underground stem 4-10 mm across ('3-lobed') matches what Isoetes treatments call a corm or pseudo-corm. PO corm is the nearest existing class. It is not the orchid pseudobulb (FLOPO_0986027), which grows above ground. The genus behind the examples should be checked.

target: spikelet (PO_0009051) with the position 'lateral' (FLOPO_0991380) as bearer state, pattern 04
reason: This is a spikelet in a lateral position, e.g. the two lateral spikelets of a Hordeum triad. It is handled like 'outer floret' (position as bearer state). Count, sterile, reduced and length go to the spikelet.

reason: This is surface sculpture of the organ described ('5-6 concentric ridges on each ventral face'), and the only quality stated is a count. It is handled the same way as 'longitudinal ridge'.
The organ that bears the appendages is not named, and the counts ('2' versus '2 - ± 50') point to different structures. 'Lateral tooth' and 'corolla appendage' were rejected for the same reason.

target: flower nectary (PO_0009056)
reason: Narrower. These are 2 separate lobes round the base of the ovary, as in Apocynaceae. When the lobes are separate, each one is a nectary, so height and a subtriangular shape belong to the nectary. Where they are lobes of a continuous disc, floral disc lobe (FLOPO_0986094) is the target. 'nectary lobe' was rejected on 2026-11-14, before floral disc lobe existed.

target: staminal tube (FLOPO_0986013)
reason: Exact: the tube of fused filaments, i.e. the staminal tube (as in Meliaceae and Malvaceae). Length and pubescence belong to the tube.

target: flower (PO_0009046) with bearer state hermaphrodite (PATO_0001340), pattern 04; in grass spikelets use spikelet floret (PO_0009082)
reason: This is the same case as 'bisexual floret' (2026-11-14). The only quality stated is a count.

target: hilum (PO_0020063), the cavity read as the hilum region of the seed or fruit; shape, size and position go to the hilum
reason: Narrower: a hollow at the hilum. Circular, small, irregular and basal describe the outline, size and position of the hilum region, so no separate class is needed.

target: stipule (PO_0020041)
reason: Narrower: interpetiolar stipules fused into a sheath, as in the Rubiaceae (Spermacoce, Hedyotis), where 'hairy, densely papillate' fits. Only in Polygonaceae is this the ochrea (FLOPO_0986040), which was the target chosen for 'stipular sheath' on 2026-11-14. This mapping goes against that earlier one; use the family to tell them apart.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020)
reason: Narrower: the bundles visible in a fruit wall ('Fruit with 3 or 4 vascular traces'). The count is a count of vascular bundles inside the organ described (container rule).

target: phyllome lamina tooth (PO_0025515)
reason: Narrower: margin teeth with a hardened tip ('3-4 callose teeth per cm'). 'Callose' is a quality of the tooth, and 'callose' on its own was judged not_a_part earlier. The phyllome tooth class covers whichever leaf or bract is meant, and the context can narrow it to leaf lamina tooth (PO_0025518).

target: plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) part of style (PO_0009074), pattern 12
reason: This is a spelling variant of 'style-base', which was handled the same way on 2026-11-14. In Cyperaceae (Eleocharis, Fimbristylis) it is the enlarged, persistent style base on the nutlet. It is not the Apiaceae stylopodium (FLOPO_0986022).

target: phyllome lamina lobe (PO_0025514) part_of leaflet (PO_0020049), pattern 12
reason: This is the same as 'leaflet segment' (2026-11-14). Narrow, acute, oblong to linear and 1-4 mm all describe the divisions of a dissected leaflet.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) part_of corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006), at the margin region
reason: These are hairs on the corolla lobe margin, handled like 'lemma hair' (trichome part_of lemma). Long, clavate, caducous and 0.5-0.8 mm all describe the hairs.
